title: I gave GPT-6 Astra a prompt I was genuinely convinced it would fumble it actually blew my mind
author: SwimOrganic8665
selftext:
Okay, so I kept seeing everyone talk about GPT-6 Astra and how much better it apparently is at actually \*building\* things.

I was skeptical.

Not in the “AI is useless” way I just feel like a lot of these insane demos look impressive until you actually try giving the model something weird and specific. 

Usually it gets the general idea right, but the details fall apart pretty quickly.

So I thought, \*\*fuck it, let me give it something unnecessarily difficult.\*\*

I asked it to build a Pokémon FireRed-style game where \*\*Super Mario replaces Red/Ash as the protagonist\*\*, but Mario also has \*\*Sonic’s abilities/powers\*\*.

Basically: Pokémon FireRed + Mario + Sonic, but actually playable.

I wasn’t expecting much. Honestly, I expected it to either simplify the idea massively, make some broken prototype, or spend half the time explaining why certain things couldn’t be done.    
Instead, it actually built the thing.

And that’s the part that caught me off guard.    
It wasn’t just generating some static mockup and calling it a game. It understood the interaction between the different systems, the visual direction, the character concept, the movement, the game structure, etc. and turned the prompt into something I could actually interact with.    
\*\*The video attached is also made by GPT-6 Astra.\*\*

What genuinely surprised me wasn’t even the fact that it could generate something like this.    
It’s how little I had to hold its hand.

A few years ago, if I wanted to make something even remotely this specific, I’d be looking at a ridiculous amount of code, assets, debugging, documentation and probably several days of work.

Now I can basically say:

“What if Pokémon FireRed had Mario as the protagonist and he had Sonic’s powers?”

…and the model goes \*\*“sure”\*\* and starts building.    
We’re getting dangerously close to the point where the limiting factor isn’t \*“can you build it?”\*    
It’s \*\*“can you come up with something worth building?”\*\*

And honestly, that’s a much crazier shift.    
I went into this trying to make GPT-6 Astra fail.    
Instead it made me rethink what I should even be asking these models to do.
